name: Ivan Rossi

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m from the independent Work Futures Panel, and what you say stays confidential. What does a normal day at the accounting firm involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and only a junior accountant, even with a bachelor’s degree in accounting; I came to preparing accounts and tax returns late and still ask about unfamiliar claims. I like the morning when a muddled receipt finally has a place, but I hate sending a return when I cannot explain one line. Eva and I have grown children who live elsewhere, and my low wage and our three weeks of savings keep retirement a question rather than a date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small change is believable; I already use AI every morning to sort tax-return questions. It often puts a receipt under the wrong heading, and I have to check it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my desk mate to keep the source receipts with each return, even when the draft arrives quickly. A clean screen is no use if the number is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Between us, I have barely three weeks of bills saved, so even the present lower pay feels narrow. There are few accounting firms near us, and I cannot shrug off a missed paid week just because retirement is on the horizon.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned returns and check the AI sorting against original receipts. On payday I would put ten from my wages into a separate emergency envelope if our food and rent bills allow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the thin margin we already live on, although I like my work. Mild AI does not pay the electricity bill if the firm has a slow month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was the last mistake you caught?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last Tuesday the tool put a pharmacy receipt into a client travel claim, and I found it before filing. I am still learning the tax rules, so I ask senior reviewer Salma when a claim looks odd.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where does the ten come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The ten comes from wages, not the three weeks already saved. If the week is short, I would skip the transfer and pay the food bill first.

say: I would keep **original receipts** beside each quick tax draft.
I would ask Salma about **odd claims** before the return goes out.
think: Three weeks of **savings** makes even ordinary low pay feel narrow.
Few nearby **accounting firms** leave little room for a missed wage.
do: Keep preparing **assigned returns** and checking daily AI sorting against receipts.
Transfer **ten from wages** on payday if food and rent bills allow.
feel: **Anxious** about the present thin cash margin.
S0.quote: A clean screen is no use if the number is wrong.
fieldNote: Ivan enjoys **daily AI sorting** but knows his junior tax judgment still needs source receipts and Salma’s second look.
His **three week reserve** and few local firms make a mild scenario financially uncomfortable before any radical change arrives.

steps.text: Keep assigned returns and check daily AI sorting against receipts
Transfer ten from wages on payday if food and rent bills allow

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The desk will feel this quickly; writing and checking are most of my shift. I have learned to use AI, but I am not yet the person who signs a difficult return alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm should count corrected errors before it cuts a junior shift. I would tell colleagues that a faster draft still needs someone to ask why a number moved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my own paid day could disappear when the new checker takes over simple returns. My partner Eva’s care wage alone would not cover our rent and groceries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my supervisor Salma for paid time to learn the new firm-approved tax checker on five closed files, with her reviewing each correction; if she agrees, I will complete them. If she refuses, I will practise on free sample returns at home and keep current paid files only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because losing a day from this wage would take food money away. I can learn quickly, but the firm has to give me paid work to use that skill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do if a paid day vanished?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my paid day is cut, I will apply for posted payroll clerk work at the clinic, but only if written pay covers our bills and the start date is confirmed before I leave. I cannot count a friendly call as a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would prove the checker works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The closed files must show whether I miss a deduction, not only whether I am faster. I would use the new checker on live returns only after Salma signs a passing error report.

say: I would ask for **error counts** before junior shifts are cut.
I would say a **fast draft** still needs someone to explain changes.
think: I expect my **paid day** could disappear under a new checker.
Eva’s care wage alone cannot meet our **rent and food**.
do: Learn the **new tax checker** on five closed files only with Salma-approved paid supervision and signed error clearance.
If hours fall, seek **posted clinic payroll work** with written bill covering pay and confirmed start; retain current paid files while offered.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing food money through a cut shift.
S1.quote: My partner Eva’s care wage alone would not cover our rent and groceries.
fieldNote: He is already a **daily AI user**, but the new checker requires actual supervised practice and an error gate before live returns.
A lost paid day triggers a **posted clinic search**; refusal of training leads to free examples and current work only while offered.

steps.text: Complete five closed-file checks in Salma-approved paid time; use live only after signed error report

If hours fall, seek posted clinic payroll job with written bill covering pay and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 would handle the thinking in tax returns before those 2031 robots matter to our desks. I would ask for the firm’s paid-work dates, not a speech.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my colleagues to insist on a written plan for junior shifts and final pay. I would not say the clinic job will still be there either.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect to lose most of my junior tax hours in the first year after AGI. Three weeks saved is not time enough to wait for another accounting firm. My partner Eva’s wage will not cover both of us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now, I would cancel the television package at renewal and send the released monthly fee into the bill account. After 2028 job loss, I would apply for posted clinic payroll or reception work only if written wages cover our rent and groceries and a start date is fixed; I would take paid firm closeout work only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed, with a plan I can name but very little room if it fails. I would need the first new pay date before the current wage stops for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill can you change before 2028?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The television package renews in March, so the cut is a real one we can make. I would tell Eva first because we both use it after work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the clinic?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The clinic is one bus ride away, which matters if we have to sell the older car. I would apply only to actual posted work, not assume the clinic owes me a place.

say: I would ask for **written junior-shift dates** as tax desk work faces AGI in 2028.
I would not claim the **clinic** has a safe job waiting.
think: I expect most of my **junior tax hours** to vanish after 2028.
Three weeks saved cannot replace my wage, and **Eva’s pay** cannot cover both of us.
do: Cancel the **television package** at March renewal and retain the released fee for bills.
Seek **posted clinic work** after job loss only with written rent-and-grocery-covering pay and a fixed start.
Take **paid closeout files** only while the firm offers them.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected loss of nearly all paid hours.
S2.quote: Three weeks saved is not time enough to wait for another accounting firm.
fieldNote: He identifies **2028 desk exposure** correctly; the later robots do not extend the life of junior tax analysis.
The **March package cut** frees current cash, while clinic applications remain conditional on posted vacancies, wages and start date.

steps.text: Cancel television package at March renewal and retain fee for bills
Take paid firm closeout files only while offered
Seek posted clinic work after 2028 loss with written rent-and-grocery-covering pay and fixed start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 gives me more evenings to practise, but AGI still reaches our screen work in 2031. The 2034 robots do not change when my returns are written.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to publish paid places for payroll training before it tells juniors to prepare. I would want to know whether a new role actually has a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn a new filing cycle, but I am 58 now and cannot assume that retirement money will cover our rent five years on. With three weeks saved, I still need a paid route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the clinic for a posted paid payroll trainee place, and take its supervised filing practice only if it offers written bill-covering wages, confirmed hours, a start date and paid training time with fees covered. If no such place opens, I will study free published payroll examples while keeping my current paid returns only while the firm offers them. In the first year after 2031, I would retain only paid training or returns still offered; if both end before a qualifying clinic offer, I would use our small reserve for bills while continuing the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because five years gives me some control, though I expect the old desk work to thin. I would not pay course fees from the food money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would proper payroll practice involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A month end means matching hours to pay and checking the filing date. I would practise the full cycle with a payroll supervisor, not just watch a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the clinic post pays too little?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will check the clinic notice board each month. A posted notice is not a wage. If a written offer does not cover rent and groceries, I keep applying while paid firm work exists.

say: I would ask for **posted paid trainee places** before juniors are told to prepare.
I would point to **2031** as the desk deadline, not the later robots.
think: I cannot assume **retirement money** will cover rent in five years.
Three weeks saved means I need a **paid learning route**.
do: Train on a **supervised payroll cycle** only with a posted clinic place, funded fees, paid time and written bill covering wage/start/shifts.
If no suitable place opens, study **free payroll examples** while assigned paid returns continue.
Keep **offered paid work** after 2031; if training and returns end, use the small reserve during the qualifying-offer search.
feel: **Anxious** about shrinking desk work, with time to search.
S3.quote: A posted notice is not a wage.
fieldNote: His **payroll route** requires an actual trainee vacancy, supervised practice, funded fees, paid time and written household covering terms.
Free examples are an **active learning fallback**, tied to current paid returns only while the firm still assigns them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade to 2036 makes me 68, but I do not know whether we could stop earning then. AGI would still reach desk returns in 2036 before hands-on robots in 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our adult children what work has taught me. A job title is no retirement plan. I would ask the firm to show staff the paid hours it expects to keep, year by year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I hope we can slow down by then, but I cannot put a number on income we have not arranged. Our rent and food have to be met from actual pay, and three weeks saved is no bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep taking assigned paid returns while they exist and transfer fifteen from wages each month into emergency cash only when bills allow. If my paid work contracts after 2036, I would apply for posted clinic reception shifts only with written pay covering rent and groceries, confirmed hours and a start date; I would not resign for a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious now because ten years helps with planning but does not create income. I would be alarmed if the firm actually stopped paying me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would that monthly saving work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Fifteen is small, but it is money not currently saved. If Eva loses hours or food costs rise, I stop the transfer and pay the immediate bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What sort of later job could fit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would prefer three predictable reception days to a grand title without wages. The clinic still has to post the role and put its hours and start in writing.

say: I would ask for **paid-hour forecasts** rather than assume a title lasts to retirement.
I would tell our adult children that **actual wages** must cover the bills.
think: I cannot count **unarranged retirement income** against rent and food.
A decade to 2036 helps, but **three weeks saved** is no bridge.

feel: **Anxious** now; alarmed if actual paid work ends.
S4.quote: A job title is no retirement plan.
fieldNote: At **68 in 2036**, he refuses to assume a pension or other retirement income that the interview has not established.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my junior hours to disappear before we build any reserve. A real posted clinic job with written pay and a start date, or a paid place to learn payroll, would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how long I want to work. I want to stop when we can pay the bills without my wage, not when a calendar says I am old enough.

headlineQuote: I want to stop when we can pay the bills without my wage, not when a calendar says I am old enough.
portrait: Ivan is a **58 year old junior** accountant with a bachelor’s degree who still asks a senior reviewer about unfamiliar tax claims.
He uses **AI daily** to sort questions but checks receipts himself and needs actual paid work to keep learning.
Eva’s care wage, grown children, **three weeks saved**, lower pay and few local firms make even the plateau anxious.
He seeks **posted clinic work** and supervised payroll practice only with written wages, funded training and a real start.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture threatens most of Ivan’s junior desk hours before he can build a reserve.
whatWouldHelp: A **posted clinic job** with written pay and start, or a paid payroll learning place, would help.
